terms.comment: Mixing alone need not imply that solid pieces have been ground smooth.

terms.gloss: mix or mingle together; throw into confusion
evidence: Caes. BG 7.62: permixtī cum suīs fugientibus (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Omnia miscē et tere, dōnec frustula nūlla supersint.
phrases.english: Mix and blend everything until no little pieces remain.
mixed up with their own men as they fled
Mix the flour and the milk together.

phrases.latin: Ōvum ūnum additō et ūnā permiscētō bene.
phrases.english: Add one egg and mix it all well together.

phrases.latin: Hunc colōrem cum illō miscē: vidēsne? Viridis fit.
phrases.english: Mix this colour with that one: see? It’s turning green.

phrases.latin: Būtȳrum cum saccharō rudiculā tere, dōnec candidum fīat.
phrases.english: Beat the butter and sugar with a wooden spoon until it turns pale.

phrases.latin: posteā inditō mellis bonī P. IIII S. id ūnā bene conmiscētō cum cāseō
phrases.english: then put in four and a half pounds of good honey, and mix it well together with the cheese
